page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and relies on a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data places this instance consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU testing, it achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1864.49 and a multi-core score of 15504.4, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9464.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 849.57 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 102.07 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 59.04 GB/sec for large-block writes.

The instance demonstrates solid capabilities for memory-bound tasks, achieving 15.46 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 7565.93 in PassMark database operations. However, compute-heavy LLM inference exposes performance limitations; while prompt processing for a small 135M model reaches 1281.58 tokens per second, a medium 7B model drops to a weak 30.95 tokens per second. This profile makes the instance suitable for database hosting, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications rather than large-scale AI inference.
